problem: Let $T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -8 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & 0 \\ -2 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}]$ be the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T.$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 8 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Im}(T).$
worked_solution:
The vector $v$ belongs to $\text{Im}(T)$ if there exists a vector $u=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]$ such that $T(u)=v.$

Therefore, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot u & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & -8 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & 0 \\ -2 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 8 \\ k\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3x-8y \\ 2x-4y \\ -2x+10y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 8 \\ k\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x-8y=6 \\ 2x-4y=8 \\ -2x+10y=k.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get $x=4+2y$, which we substitute into the first equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-8y & =6 \\ 3(4+2y)-8y & =6 \\ -2y & =-6 \\ y & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =4+2y \\  & =4+2(3) \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=10$ and $y=3$ into the third equation and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+10y & =k \\ -2(10)+10(3) & =k \\ k & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $v\in \text{Im}(T)$ when $k=10.$
